claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: Adding ℓ−k isolated K2 components with their endpoints as new terminal pairs gives an exact equivalence: every new path is forced to be its isolated edge, while original paths cannot enter those components. Since H3 is connected and has eight vertices, the union is H3-free exactly when the original instance is. For k=1, connectivity suffices because a shortest terminal-to-terminal path has no chord; BFS or DFS decides this in O(n+m). For fixed k, at most k simple vertex sequences of length at most n form a polynomial certificate, and all path, disjointness, chord, and cross-adjacency conditions are polynomially checkable.
claims.witness: The padding gadget for each additional pair is one isolated edge K2.
claims.search_method: Direct reduction and certificate analysis from the source definition; no external material used.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: If dist(u,v)=3 with geodesic u-x-y-v and both endpoints have degree at least three, choose two additional neighbors at each endpoint. Geodesicity excludes all connector vertices from these choices and excludes overlap between the two pairs, since a shared neighbor would give distance at most two. These eight distinct vertices and the seven required edges form H3 as a subgraph. For degeneracy, every graph of minimum degree at least seven contains every eight-vertex tree by a parent-before-child greedy embedding: when embedding the jth vertex, at most j−2≤6 neighbors of its parent's image are already occupied. Therefore every subgraph of an H3-free graph has a vertex of degree at most six. A 6-degeneracy ordering gives at most 6(n−7)+21=6n−21 edges for n≥7. K7 is H3-free by order and has degeneracy six. Finally, four consecutive vertices of any geodesic of length at least three contradict the distance lemma when minimum degree is at least three.
claims.witness: K7 witnesses sharpness of the degeneracy constant and equality in the stated bound at n=7.

claims.claim: The induced-path fan threshold is seven edges: if an induced path in an H3-free graph has at least seven edges and every internal vertex has degree at least three, then every internal vertex has degree exactly three and all internal vertices have the same unique neighbor outside the path. Consequently, every run of at least six consecutive internal degree-at-least-three vertices on an arbitrary induced path is a fan about one off-path vertex.
claims.evidence: For p0…p7 let O_i be the nonempty off-path neighborhood of p_i, 1≤i≤6. For i=1,2,3, distinct a∈O_i and b∈O_{i+3} would make p_i-p_{i+1}-p_{i+2}-p_{i+3} the H3 connector, with leaves p_{i−1},a and p_{i+4},b. Hence O_i and O_{i+3} are the same singleton. Write the three resulting singleton values as a,b,c. If a≠b, connector p1-a-p4-p5 with leaves p0,p2 and p6,b gives H3; if b≠c, connector p2-b-p5-p6 with leaves p1,p3 and p7,c gives H3. Thus a=b=c. Inducedness excludes other on-path neighbors, so every internal degree is exactly three. Applying this argument to each consecutive seven-edge window of a longer induced path covers all internal vertices; overlapping windows share internal vertices with a unique third neighbor, forcing their hubs to coincide. Six consecutive internal high-degree vertices plus their two path neighbors form exactly such a window.
claims.witness: The local p0…p7 argument supplies an explicit H3 whenever any required off-path-neighbor equality fails.
claims.search_method: Direct exhaustive case proof at the seven-edge boundary, followed by overlapping-window propagation. The finite checker additionally exhausts all 203 identifications of one designated off-path neighbor for the six internal vertices.

claims.claim: The seven-edge threshold, and equivalently the six-vertex run threshold, is best possible.
claims.evidence: On induced path p0-p1-p2-p3-p4-p5-p6, add h adjacent exactly to p1,p2,p4,p5 and q adjacent exactly to p3. All five internal path vertices have degree three, but p3 has off-path neighbor q whereas the others have h, so the fan conclusion fails one edge and one internal vertex below the theorem. The exact checker enumerates every simple three-edge connector with eligible endpoints and all possible disjoint leaf choices; it finds 20 connector paths up to reversal and no H3 embedding.
claims.search_method: Constructed boundary counterexample followed by exact finite H3-subgraph enumeration.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: Every subdivision vertex has degree two, so an H3 center would have to be original. A simple three-edge path starting at an original vertex either takes three steps inside a four-edge R-corridor and ends at a subdivision vertex, or first uses M and then—because M is a matching—must take two corridor steps and again ends at a subdivision vertex. Thus no possible centers are joined by a three-edge path. A path with original endpoints cannot enter only part of a corridor: its internal vertices have degree two, so the whole corridor is traversed. Contracting and expanding used corridors therefore bijects simple host paths with base paths. Internally disjoint corridors create no extra selected-vertex adjacencies. The only possible chords or edges between lifted paths are unsubdivided M-edges, and exactly the stated consecutive-use condition eliminates them. With M empty and R=K_m, contracting every corridor yields a K_m minor, proving unbounded treewidth.
claims.witness: Taking M empty and R=K_m gives an H3-free graph containing K_m as a minor for every m.
claims.search_method: Direct degree-and-distance proof, exact contraction/lifting analysis, and bounded exhaustive corroboration over all R and compatible M on at most five original vertices.

claims.claim: In the routing-plus-matching normal form, matching edges cannot be treated as forbidden pairs even when the routing graph is just two disjoint paths: there is an H3-free two-pair instance whose straight rail routes violate the matching conflicts but whose paths switch rails through four matching edges and form an induced linkage.
claims.evidence: The four displayed cross-rail edges form a matching. The straight rail paths select both endpoints of every matching edge on different paths, so they are not mutually induced. The switched base paths use respectively matching edges a1b2,a4b3 and a2b1,a3b4; together they use every matching edge whose endpoints are selected. All other steps are rail edges and lift through distinct four-edge corridors. The lifted paths are vertex-disjoint, individually induced, and have no cross-edge. The exact checker constructs the 42-vertex host, verifies H3-freeness, rejects the straight linkage, and accepts the switched linkage.
claims.witness: R consists of rails a0…a5 and b0…b5; M={a1b2,a2b1,a3b4,a4b3}; switched paths are a0-a1-b2-b3-a4-a5 and b0-b1-a2-a3-b4-b5.
claims.search_method: Direct edge-by-edge verification and exact finite graph checking.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: After deleting B, every component has maximum degree two. A path component has at most two attachment edges, since only its endpoints can attach to B; a cycle has none. A terminal-free component used by a solution must be traversed completely between two distinct B vertices. Components with fewer usable attachments or two attachments to the same B cannot occur in a simple terminal path, and one representative suffices for each unordered pair of distinct B vertices. In a terminal-bearing path or cycle component, mark every terminal and B-attachment occurrence. Each unmarked gap has no external neighbors and is either traversed completely or avoided. Preserving a one-edge gap and replacing every longer gap by a two-edge path preserves precisely both traversal and direct-adjacency behavior, so expansion and contraction preserve all linkage conditions. Terminal-free tails are unusable; a detached cycle with one terminal is a NO component. There are b retained branching vertices, at most 2k terminal vertices, at most binom(b,2) generic corridor vertices, and at most 4k gap vertices: a path component with t≥1 terminals has at most t+1≤2t gaps, while a cycle has t. Hence the total is at most b+binom(b,2)+6k. Brute-force solution of this bounded graph and certificate expansion give FPT time.
claims.witness: The compression proof supplies inverse expansion and contraction maps for every retained corridor and marked gap.
claims.search_method: Direct component decomposition, preservation proof, vertex count, and parameterized running-time analysis.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: The host is H3-free because H3 has eight vertices. Exact simple-path enumeration finds only s1-x-t1 and s1-y-z-t1, making the former the unique shortest route. Since the second path contains its endpoint s2 and xs2 is an edge, the shortest route cannot belong to an induced linkage. Conversely, s1-y-z-t1 and s2-t2 are induced, vertex-disjoint, and anticomplete to one another.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of all simple s1-t1 paths and direct linkage validation.

target_evidence: The source target requires a complexity classification for every fixed k. The draft correctly settles only the trivial k=1 case and proves structural, counterexample, normal-form, and parameterized results; it proves neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor NP-hardness for any fixed k≥2. These are material correct advances but do not resolve the requested classification. Its explicit claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is therefore accurate.
